children: Civil Aviation Minister K Rammohan Naidu said the government will assess the pros and cons of allowing airport operators to own stakes in airlines, with no decision taken yet

The government will examine whether airport operators should be allowed to own stakes in airlines, Civil Aviation Minister K Rammohan Naidu said on Tuesday, as India seeks to expand airline capacity alongside a growing airport network.

The proposal will be assessed before the government takes a decision, Naidu said. He added that the government’s priority is to increase the number of airlines and provide passengers with more choices as air travel demand expands.
Naidu said India should target at least five airlines with fleets of 100 aircraft each, while also building an airport network of more than 350 airports over the longer term.

According to media reports, the signing of agreements for the next phase of the Udan regional connectivity scheme, Naidu said the government would assess the “pros and cons” of airport operators owning stakes in airlines. He said the objective would be to take a balanced approach while ensuring that the aviation sector has enough airline capacity to meet demand.

The minister’s comments follow a proposal seeking relaxation of restrictions governing cross-ownership between airports and airlines. The issue has gained attention after Adani Airports approached the Airports Authority of India seeking a waiver from a contractual provision that restricts airport operators at Mumbai from holding more than a 10 per cent stake in a scheduled airline.
Adani Enterprises, however, said in July that it was not evaluating a proposal to enter the airline business, describing reports of a planned airline as baseless and factually incorrect.

The restrictions at the Delhi and Mumbai airports arise from their Operation, Management and Development Agreements, or OMDAs, signed when the airports were transferred to private operators under the public-private partnership model. Reporting on the existing framework indicates that the agreements restrict the relevant airport operators and their group entities from taking substantial ownership in scheduled airlines.

The government has previously clarified that there is no blanket government policy prohibiting airport operators from operating airlines. The restrictions are contained in contractual arrangements governing certain PPP airports, including Delhi and Mumbai.

Naidu said the expansion of airline capacity is necessary to make use of rising demand for air travel across the country. He said India needs at least five airlines operating fleets of 100 aircraft each to meet the requirements of the market.

He also linked the expansion of airlines to the development of airport infrastructure, saying the government is supporting the creation of a larger aviation network. According to Naidu, demand for airports is no longer limited to major cities, with passengers in smaller towns also seeking nearby air connectivity.
India should ideally have more than 350 airports as part of its longer-term aviation infrastructure plans, Naidu said, adding that planning needs to account for the country's objectives for 2047.

The minister's comments come as the government works on the next phase of Udan, the regional connectivity programme, while also seeking to expand India's airport and airline capacity. As of 30 June 2026, the Civil Aviation Ministry's data showed 95 airports, including heliports and water aerodromes, under the Udan scheme, with 677 routes and nine operators.
